notes.decision: Translated 'goodness' from Greek καλωσύνη (with prosthetic ⲁ-). Reading uncertain — letters dotted in transcription. Alternative ἀκακοσύνη 'innocence/guilelessness' is also possible if reading ⲁⲕⲁⲕⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ. Either fits the moral-ascetic register.

Translated 'wearing' — ⲣ̄-ⲫⲟⲣⲉⲓ from Greek φορεῖν 'to wear, bear'; ⲛ- prefix forms a circumstantial 'as a wearer'. The Mind of Light dons the small body of flesh as a garment — standard Manichaean christological motif.

Translated 'is in oppression' — ⲫⲗⲓⲃⲉ from Greek θλίβειν 'press, afflict, oppress'. The cosmic gods stationed in the body are themselves 'in affliction' — the Manichaean motif of divine suffering for the sake of light-extraction. ⲟ̄ⲛⲟⲩ functions as locative-stative marker.

Provisionally rendered 'supports/foundations'. Lexeme not in standard Coptic dictionaries; the trees-with-roots image dominant in lines 6-8 suggests a noun denoting what holds something fast in place. Possibly cognate with ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp, hold' (qualitative ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧ). Flagged for future parallel research.

Tentatively rendered '[reaching] upward' — the directional ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' is clear, but ⲉϩⲃⲓ̈ is uncertain. Possibly Lyc form of a verb of extension/reaching, or an adverbial of motion-up. The line continues into a lost portion of line 10.

Translated 'this Living Spirit' — Manichaean cosmological figure (the Great Architect/Builder), whose five sons bind the soul into the body. The 'his members' (ⲛⲉϩⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ) are the cosmic limbs through which he operates.

Translated 'Sin took this body forth'. ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ here is capitalized as the cosmic principle 'Sin' per terminology guide. The act parallels the cosmogonic seizure-of-body that follows in lines 14-17 where the Living Spirit re-establishes the body from the five dark bodies.

Translated 'the five Gods that are radiant' — ⲡⲣⲱⲩ qualitative of ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate'. Per correspondential principle, retained the active-emission verb-quality ('radiant' over 'shining' or 'bright'). The Five Sons of the Living Spirit are the radiant ones from whom the soul is taken forth before being bound in the body.

The five members of the body in correspondence with the five faculties: bone↔mind, sinew↔thought, vein↔teaching, flesh↔counsel, skin↔reflection. Each correspondence is a direct identity in the Manichaean register, not a comparison.
Translated 'foremost of the powers' — ⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ 'foremost rank' (from glossary) + ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'powers' (Lyc plural of ϫⲟⲙ). Refers to the Living Spirit's mind set at the head of the soul's faculties.

Tentatively translated 'they oppress the soul' — ⲭⲗⲟⲩⲱ unidentified, possibly Lyc reflex of ϫⲱⲗ 'twist, deceive, violate' or related to a constraint-verb. The context (the dark powers drawing the soul to evil works) requires a negative-action verb on the soul. Confidence low; flagged for parallel research.

Translated 'the practice that stands fast' — ⲙⲛⲧⲟⲁⲟⲩⲁⲛ from glossary ('practice/comportment') + qualitative ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲥ̄ 'stands fast'. Refers to the established/instituted practice of idol-worship to which the souls are humbled.

Tentatively rendered 'they make use' — ⲟ̄ⲁⲭⲏ may be Greek ἀρχή 'rule, beginning, principle' with ⲣ̄- 'do'. Could mean 'exercise rule/practice' but reading uncertain. Context: serving the beasts/animals (zoolatry) follows.
